listing.title: Sourdough Season Shirt, Watercolor Sourdough Bread Tee, Sourdough Baker Gift, Bread Baking T-Shirt, Starter Jar and Boule Shirt
listing.description: A cozy bake-day still life painted in watercolor: a round sourdough boule dusted with flour, its curved score opened into a dark-baked ear above a row of little wheat-ear cuts, a glass jar of bubbly starter that has doubled past its rubber band, two slices with an open crumb resting on a blue-striped linen towel, a round wooden bread board, and two bunches of golden wheat, under "Sourdough Season" in painted lettering. A gift for the home baker who keeps a starter going all winter. Small gold sparkles finish the scene.

listing.trademark_check: Legal Desk screen 2026-11-27 (before any art): web searches '"SOURDOUGH SEASON" trademark', 'SOURDOUGH trademark clothing t-shirts justia', 'sourdough trademark uspto.report class 25 shirts', and follow-ups on the three sourdough records that turned up with clothing or bread goods (tmsearch.uspto.gov is blocked from our sessions, so the Justia search-result summaries were read). No record for the phrase SOURDOUGH SEASON turned up, and no shirt titled 'Sourdough Season' was found for sale. Nearest: SOURDOUGH LIFESTYLE (serial 97544192, pending, filed 2022-08-11) covers shirts, sweatshirts, hats and stickers; THE SOURDOUGH COOKIE COMPANY (serial 98828932, pending, filed 2024-10-30) covers tops and headwear; SOURDOUGH (serial 75577535, Snyder's of Delaware) covers pretzels only. Other sourdough marks (SOURDOUGH SAM, MRS. SOURDOUGH, EPIC SOURDOUGH with 'sourdough' disclaimed) cover bakery goods or services. 'Sourdough' is the generic name of the bread, so the art uses it only as a description, in the shop's 'X Season' pattern (Soup, Cocoa, Tea Season), never alone as a brand label. Kept out of the art, titles and tags: 'lifestyle', 'cookie company', 'Mr./Mrs. Sourdough', the slogans seen on sale ('In My Sourdough Era', 'Wake and Bake', 'Sourdough Mama', 'Feed It. Use It. Chill It. Repeat.', 'I Have a Starter and Boundaries') and the Real Bread Campaign's 'Sourdough September'. No brand, show, character or celebrity names.
